metaDescription: Five flexible bathtub drain brushes compared by reach, bristle width, and kit contents, so you can clear hair and soap scum without calling a plumber.
introParagraphs: A slow tub drain is usually a hair and soap scum problem, and the cheapest fix is a flexible brush that reaches below the strainer. The five picks here span a wide range of reach, from the TAICHODEER kit with two 16.7 inch brushes to the SPESHALU at 67 inches and the Bozenu set with a 66 inch main brush plus a 58 inch pipe brush. Head diameters run from 0.5 inches up to 1.26 inches, which matters more than most listings admit.

We evaluated each brush based on product specs and buyer feedback, looking at how far it reaches, how wide the bristle heads are, what the shaft is made of, and how much you get in the box. The BaBaYang and cuitrent are single brushes marketed for several drains, while the Bozenu, SPESHALU, and TAICHODEER are drain focused kits. Two of the listings state no length at all, so we say so plainly instead of guessing.

Most buyers in our audience want something simple to use with wet hands, easy to rinse, and easy to put away. That favors a brush you can steer without kneeling or wrestling a five foot coil, but it also means being honest about reach: a short brush cleans the strainer area and nothing deeper. Use the tables below to match your drain, your tub finish, and your storage space to a specific pick.

products.name: Bozenu Flexible Drain Brush Set
products.description:
The Bozenu set earns the top slot because it is the only kit here that hands you three separate long brushes instead of one. The main tool is a 66 inch double ended brush with 0.6 inch and 1.2 inch bristle heads, so you can use the narrow end in a tight overflow tube and the wide end in the main tub drain. A second 58 inch pipe brush with a 0.5 inch head covers the slimmest passages in the same bundle.

The listing describes food grade, rust resistant material and soft but durable nylon bristles, which is a sensible combination for a tool that lives in a damp bathroom. The method is simple: insert it, swirl, pull it out, and rinse. Because the bristles are soft, they are gentler on a tub finish than a stiff wire head, although they will need more passes on caked soap scum than a firmer brush would.

Setup is just rinsing the brushes and hanging them to dry, but three long brushes do mean finding a place for more than five feet of wire. The two 8 inch straw brushes are handy for the overflow cover and small fixture openings. Compared with the SPESHALU set, whose main brush is only about one inch longer, the Bozenu adds an entire extra 58 inch brush, which makes it the better all around bundle.
products.bestFor: Households that want one kit to cover the main drain, the overflow tube, and narrow pipes

Three head widths from 0.5 to 1.2 inches
Soft nylon bristles are gentle on finishes
Two small straw brushes included
cons: More than five feet of wire to store
Soft bristles need extra passes on hard scum
Takes more storage space than a single brush

products.name: TAICHODEER 3 Piece Drain Brush Kit
products.description:
The TAICHODEER kit takes the opposite approach from the 60 plus inch coils: two 16.7 inch flexible brushes plus a crevice brush in a three piece set. The thick brush measures 1.26 inches across and the slim one 0.6 inches, so one handles the wide drain opening while the other fits narrower gaps. The crevice brush adds a tool for edges, fixtures, and the seam where the drain meets the tub floor.

Those lengths define who should buy it. They reach the strainer area and the first stretch of pipe below it, which is where most hair collects, but they will not travel to a deep trap the way the Bozenu or SPESHALU coils can. The upside is control, since a short brush is easier to steer, easier to grip with wet hands, and faster to use on a weekly rinse.

Ownership is easy because the three pieces fit in a drawer or a shower caddy without tangling. There is no long coil to unwind, which suits anyone who finds a coil more than five feet long awkward to manage. If your drain has a standard stopper and you only want to keep the top section clear, this is the tidier choice, while the Bozenu is the one to buy if you want to chase clogs further down.
products.bestFor: Light weekly upkeep of the drain opening and fixture crevices
pros: Three pieces including a crevice brush
Two widths at 1.26 and 0.6 inches
Short length is easy to steer and store
Fits a drawer without tangling
cons: At 16.7 inches it cannot reach a deep trap
Listing does not state the shaft material
Fewer bristle sizes than the Bozenu kit

products.name: SPESHALU 67 Inch Flexible Drain Brush
products.description:
The SPESHALU brush has the longest reach in this roundup at 67 inches of stainless steel. The listing says it is flexible enough to pass a U bend, which matters because the trap is where hair and soap scum tend to settle. Each end carries a bristle head 2.5 inches long, one at 0.6 and one at 1.2 diameter, and two 8 inch straw brushes come along for smaller openings.

The reach comes at a premium price relative to the other picks, and that is the main reason it sits third rather than first. You get one long double ended brush rather than the extra pipe brush that Bozenu includes, so the extra cost buys length and a stainless build, not a bigger bundle. The stainless wire is durable, but a metal core does deserve care at the tub drain opening, where dragging it across the finish can scuff acrylic or fiberglass.

In practice, feed it in slowly, twist as you push, pull it back out with the bristles gripping debris, and rinse it before it dries. Store it in a loose coil rather than a tight loop, which keeps the wire from taking a permanent kink. Next to the Bozenu main brush the SPESHALU is only about one inch longer, so choose it for the stainless build and the longest reach, not for a meaningful gain in distance.
products.bestFor: Deep clogs past the U bend where every extra inch of reach counts
pros: 67 inches is the longest reach here
Stainless steel build is durable
Listing says it passes a U bend
Two 8 inch straw brushes included
cons: Premium price for one main brush

products.name: BaBaYang Drain and Lint Brush

specList.label: Uses
specList.value: Sink, tub, shower drains and dryer vents

products.description:
The BaBaYang brush is the multi purpose option, and it costs less than most of the drain specific kits here. It pairs a bendable stainless steel shaft with dense spiral bristles, a design the listing says resists bending while still clearing hair, soap scum, and debris from tubs, showers, and kitchen sinks. The same tool is also sold for dryer vents and refrigerator coils, so it can earn its keep outside the bathroom.

That versatility has a cost in focus. The listing does not state the overall length or bristle diameter, so you cannot size it against your pipe the way you can with the Bozenu or TAICHODEER measurements. It is a single brush, which means one head width has to handle every drain in the house.

Ownership is straightforward because a single spiral brush rinses clean under a tap and hangs on a hook. Dryer lint is dry and fluffy while drain gunk is wet and greasy, so wash and dry it thoroughly between jobs if you plan to use it on both. Compared with the cuitrent, the other single brush in this group, the BaBaYang is the one to pick if you also want a lint and coil tool, while the cuitrent is the simpler drain only choice.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers who want one brush for the tub, the sink, and the dryer vent
pros: Lowest cost of the five picks
Bendable stainless shaft with spiral bristles
Also cleans dryer vents and fridge coils
One piece is simple to rinse and hang
cons: Length and bristle width are not listed
A single head size cannot suit every drain
Dual use needs careful washing between jobs

products.name: cuitrent Flexible Drain Brush
products.description:
The cuitrent is a plain, single flexible brush aimed at sinks, showers, and drain pipes. The listing says the long flexible head bends freely to reach deep corners inside pipes and narrow gaps, which is the behavior you want when the pipe turns right under the drain. It sits in the middle of the price range, so it is neither the cheapest pick nor the premium one.

What it does not give you is detail. No length, no bristle diameter, and no set of extras are listed, so you are buying on the general design rather than on measurable specs. That is fine for a single bathroom you want to keep running, but it is harder to recommend than the Bozenu when you cannot confirm that it will reach past the trap.

Using it is the familiar routine of push in, twist, pull out, and rinse. Plan to wear a glove for the pull, because what comes out is usually hair wrapped in soap film. If you want certainty about size, the TAICHODEER lists both diameters, and if you want the bonus lint tool, the BaBaYang is the better single brush.
products.bestFor: One bathroom that needs a simple, no fuss brush for occasional drain care

Mid range price among the five

buyingCriteria.explanation: Length decides whether you clear only the strainer area or the trap below it. The SPESHALU reaches 67 inches and the Bozenu offers a 66 inch main brush plus a 58 inch pipe brush, while the TAICHODEER kit tops out at 16.7 inches per brush. A good rule is that a short brush handles hair near the strainer, but if water still drains slowly after the strainer is clear, you need a brush of roughly 60 inches or more to get past the U bend. Do not buy more length than you will actually use, because a coil of more than five feet is harder to handle and store.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Bristle head diameter versus pipe size
buyingCriteria.explanation: A head that is too narrow glides past debris instead of grabbing it. The picks here range from the 0.5 inch head on the Bozenu pipe brush to the 1.26 inch head on the TAICHODEER, with the SPESHALU and Bozenu main brushes covering 0.6 and 1.2 inches. Choose a head that is slightly wider than the opening so the bristles touch the pipe walls as you twist. A kit with two or three widths, like the Bozenu, saves you from guessing, which is the reason single brushes such as the cuitrent and BaBaYang are riskier when they do not list a diameter.

The SPESHALU and BaBaYang use stainless steel, which is durable but stiff compared with a nylon only head. Cleaning guidance for acrylic and fiberglass tubs favors soft bristles and non scratch contact because those finishes scuff easily. In practice, keep the metal part of the shaft from dragging across the tub floor at the drain opening, and feed the brush straight down. If your tub is acrylic or fiberglass, the soft nylon bristles on the Bozenu set are the gentler fit.

Softer bristles are kinder to the surfaces you touch, while denser or firmer bristles move stubborn scum faster. The Bozenu uses soft but durable nylon, and the BaBaYang uses dense spiral bristles that are built for hair and lint. A sensible rule is to start with the softest option that works and step up only if grime persists. If you find a soft brush needs three or four passes, repeat the twist and pull cycle rather than forcing the brush deeper.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Kit contents versus a single brush
buyingCriteria.explanation: The Bozenu gives you four tools in one bundle, namely the 66 inch brush, the 58 inch brush, and two 8 inch straw brushes. The TAICHODEER gives three pieces including a crevice brush, while the BaBaYang and cuitrent are single brushes. More pieces cost more storage space, but they also mean you can match a tool to the opening instead of improvising. If you only ever clean one tub drain, a single brush is enough, and if you have a tub with a separate overflow tube, favor a kit.

A drain brush comes out coated in hair and soap film, so how easily it rinses matters as much as how well it cleans. A single spiral brush like the BaBaYang rinses fast under a tap, while the Bozenu and SPESHALU coils need a larger rinse area and a loose hanging loop. Store long coils loosely so the wire does not kink, and let every brush dry fully before putting it away. If you plan to share the BaBaYang between a drain and a dryer vent, wash it between jobs so wet gunk never meets dry lint.

howWeEvaluated.title: Reach and trap access
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the stated length of every brush, from the TAICHODEER at 16.7 inches up to the SPESHALU at 67 inches. Reach was scored on whether the listing supports getting past the U bend, since that is where most slow drains are caused. Brushes with no stated length, such as the cuitrent and BaBaYang, were scored conservatively because we could not verify the claim.

howWeEvaluated.title: Head sizing and coverage
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at the bristle diameters each listing publishes, which run from 0.5 inches on the Bozenu pipe brush to 1.26 inches on the TAICHODEER. A kit that offers more than one head width scored higher than a single head, because it adapts to different pipe openings. The Bozenu covers three widths while the cuitrent lists none, which is the widest gap in this category.

howWeEvaluated.title: Materials and finish safety
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed what the shaft and bristles are made from and how that affects a tub finish. Stainless steel on the SPESHALU and BaBaYang scored well for durability but lower for scratch risk, while the soft nylon on the Bozenu scored best for gentleness. Where a listing did not state the material, as with the TAICHODEER and cuitrent, we said so and held back full marks.

howWeEvaluated.title: Kit completeness
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted the usable tools in each package and judged whether they cover a typical bathroom. The Bozenu is the strongest here with four tools, while the cuitrent is the most basic with a single brush and no listed extras. Bundles that included small straw brushes or a crevice tool earned credit for handling overflow tubes and fixture edges.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ease of use and upkeep
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered how easy each brush is to steer, rinse, and store for someone with limited grip strength or reach. Short kits like the TAICHODEER score highest for handling, and long coils like the SPESHALU score lower but earn it back in reach. Value for money was weighed last and lightly, using only relative price tiers within this group.

cards.label: Long coil
cards.text: The Bozenu (66 and 58 inches) and SPESHALU (67 inches) reach past the trap and clear deep buildup. The cost is storage space and a bit more effort to feed and pull back without kinking.

cards.label: Short brush
cards.text: The TAICHODEER (two 16.7 inch brushes) is easy to steer and store, and it handles hair near the strainer. It cannot reach a deep trap, so it is maintenance, not rescue.

cards.label: Our recommendation
cards.text: Pick the Bozenu if you have ever had a slow drain that a strainer cleanup did not fix. Pick the TAICHODEER if you only want to keep a healthy drain healthy.

howToChoose.note: Keep any metal shaft from dragging across the tub floor at the drain opening.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A brush that is at least 60 inches long, a head width that touches the pipe walls, and bristles dense enough to catch hair. Slow tub drains are almost always hair wrapped in soap scum sitting at or just past the strainer and in the trap.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Bozenu set fits best because its 66 inch brush reaches the trap and its 0.6 and 1.2 inch heads cover both common opening sizes. If you want the extra inch and a stainless build, the SPESHALU is the alternative.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have a long pipe run or a deep trap, in which case the SPESHALU 67 inch stainless brush is worth the premium. Also spend more on the Bozenu kit if you have an overflow tube and want three head widths in one box.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only clear hair near the strainer, so the TAICHODEER short kit or the lower cost BaBaYang does the job. Save with the cuitrent if you want a basic flexible brush and plan to replace it when it wears out.

faq.q: How do I choose between a long coil and a short drain brush?
faq.a: Think about where your clogs form. If hair gathers at the strainer and just below it, a short kit like the TAICHODEER at 16.7 inches is easier to handle. If water stays slow after you clean the strainer, the clog is deeper, and a long brush such as the Bozenu or SPESHALU is the right tool.

faq.q: How much should I spend on a drain brush?
faq.a: These are low cost tools, and the price difference within this group mostly reflects length and kit contents. The BaBaYang is the lowest cost pick, the Bozenu gives the most tools per package, and the SPESHALU is the premium option for maximum reach. Spend more only if you actually need the longer reach.

faq.q: How long does a drain brush last?
faq.a: Durability depends on bristle stiffness and how often you use it. Stainless shafts like those on the SPESHALU and BaBaYang resist wear well, while nylon bristles gradually splay with use. Rinse it after each use, let it dry fully, and replace it when the bristles stop gripping hair.

faq.q: Will a drain brush scratch my bathtub?
faq.a: It can if a metal shaft drags across an acrylic or fiberglass finish, because those surfaces scuff easily. Feed the brush straight down the drain and keep the shaft off the tub floor. The soft nylon bristles on the Bozenu are the gentlest option here.

faq.q: Can I use the same brush in the tub and the kitchen sink?
faq.a: Several listings, including the cuitrent and BaBaYang, say they work on sink, shower, and tub drains. For hygiene, many people prefer a separate brush for the kitchen, since grease and food residue are different from hair. If you share one brush, rinse it thoroughly and let it dry between uses.

faq.q: Does a brush replace drain cleaner or a plumber?
faq.a: A brush removes hair and soap scum mechanically, which handles the most common cause of a slow tub drain without chemicals. It will not clear a root intrusion or a collapsed pipe. If the water stays slow after several passes with a long brush like the Bozenu, a plumber is the next step.

faq.q: How do I know what size head my drain needs?
faq.a: Look at the drain opening and choose a head slightly wider than it, so the bristles brush the pipe walls as you twist. Kits with several widths, like the Bozenu with 0.5, 0.6, and 1.2 inch heads, remove the guesswork. If you buy a single brush with no listed diameter, such as the cuitrent, plan to confirm the fit when it arrives.
